description: Team Penguins is building EarthTrend for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 in Sylhet. Using NASA data and Python, we explore global soil-moisture trends, focusing on Bangladesh through interactive maps and data-driven insights.
summary: Amar Foshol (আমার ফসল) is a Bangla-first climate-advisory prototype for farmers in Bangladesh, built for the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge. Farmers choose a district and a main crop and see simple charts and plain-language explanations in Bangla or English. The Climate Explorer uses real NASA POWER daily data for six districts (Dhaka, Rajshahi, Khulna, Rangpur, Barishal, Sylhet), showing 2010-2024 averages for temperature, very hot days (35 °C or more), yearly and monthly rainfall, and the start of heavy rain. Each card shows its source and retrieval date. A Crop Rotation section compares three illustrative pathways against farmer priorities, and a Messaging section previews WhatsApp and SMS advice. Soil moisture, vegetation, sowing-window and rotation values are clearly labeled demo or illustrative, not research findings. The site states its limits and tells farmers to consult local agriculture officers. Our goal is to make NASA climate data understandable in local language.
details:
PROBLEM: Farmers in Bangladesh plan around traditional calendars, but rainfall timing and heat are changing, and NASA climate data is technical and in English.

WHAT IT DOES: A bilingual (Bangla/English) website. A farmer picks a district (Dhaka, Rajshahi, Khulna, Rangpur, Barishal, Sylhet) and a main crop (for example Boro rice). The Climate Explorer shows temperature, very hot days (daily maximum of 35 °C or more), yearly and monthly rainfall, and the start of heavy rain. A Crop Rotation section compares three illustrative pathways against the farmer's priorities. A Messaging section previews how the advice could reach farmers by WhatsApp and SMS.

NASA DATA USED: Real data comes from NASA POWER's free daily API (v2.10.3, community AG): T2M, T2M_MAX and PRECTOTCORR, for one point at the centre of each district, averaged over 2010-2024. A script (scripts/fetch_nasa_power.py) was run once on 15 November 2026 and saved the results to a file the site reads; there is no live NASA connection. Each real value has a "Verified Source" badge and retrieval date. We show averages only, with no then-vs-now comparison, because older POWER years at these points show jumps (around 1997 and 2016) from changes in NASA's input data sources, not real climate change. Values are estimates for one map grid cell, not weather-station readings.

WHAT IS DEMO: Soil moisture, vegetation (NDVI), Boro sowing-window shifts, crop-rotation scores and the WhatsApp/SMS messages are labeled demo or illustrative; they are not research findings or field measurements. SMAP, GPM/IMERG, MODIS/VIIRS/Landsat, SRTM, ECOSTRESS and GRACE appear on a Data Sources page as planned or not connected. U.S.-only resources on the challenge page do not describe Bangladesh and are not used.

IMPACT AND NEXT STEPS: Help farmers and extension officers understand local climate in their own language.

Next: more NASA datasets, a consistent earlier period, local soil and crop data, expert-verified rotation evidence, and real WhatsApp/SMS delivery. The site tells users to consult local agriculture officers.

TOOLS AND AI USE: Claude Code, hosted on Vercel; Python for data retrieval. Claude helped write the website code and documentation. The idea, demo recording and voiceover are the team's own. Some AI-generated images are included in the Video & Websites(icons).
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources), daily API, community AG: T2M, T2M_MAX, PRECTOTCORR
projectRefs: Claude (Anthropic), AI assistant used for code and documentation
